sections.title: uses of the infinitive with to

reference.title: Uses of the infinitive with to
rows: after some verbs (want, need, would like, etc.)
You need to be on time. Try not to talk too much.
It’ll be nice to meet new people. It’s important not to be late.
after question words (what, where, how, etc.)
I don’t know where to go or what to do.
to say why you do something
Why did you wear a suit? To make a good impression.

reference.title: Negative infinitive
reference.text: not to + verb: Try not to be late. It’s important not to talk too much.

reference.title: Infinitive without to
reference.text: After auxiliary verbs (do / does / didn’t) and most modal verbs (can, could, will, would, etc.) use the infinitive without to: Do you like it? I can’t come. I’ll help you.

reference.wrong: I came to this school for learn English.
reference.right: I came to this school to learn English.
reference.why: To say why, use to + infinitive, not for.

reference.right: I don’t know what to do.

tasks.instruction: Communication: How to survive… Tell your partner the tips from your article. Then listen to your partner’s tips and decide together which tip is the most important
tasks.note: SB 3e + Communication 7A (A p.104, B p.110): ученик — A (статья о встрече с родителями партнёра — в context), ИИ — B (первое свидание; текст B не переписан — ИИ даёт пять советов по заголовку)
tasks.context:
How to survive meeting your partner’s parents for the first time
1 Do some ‘homework’ before you go. Ask your partner about his or her parents. Where do they work? Do you have any common interests? If you do this, it will be easy to have a conversation with them.
2 Be ready to answer questions about yourself! Most parents want to know about their son or daughter’s future partner, for example about their ambitions. Try to make a good impression!
3 If you are invited for a meal, eat everything! It’s also a good idea to say something positive about the meal, like ‘This is absolutely delicious!’ Offer to help with the washing-up after the meal.
4 Be yourself and don’t just agree with everything they say. If they ask you for your opinion, be honest. However, try not to talk about controversial subjects – this isn’t the moment to give your views on religion and politics!
5 Avoid embarrassing silences. If the conversation is dying and you can’t think what to say, ask them what your partner was like as a child. All parents love talking about their children.

exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate), Student B in a pair activity. The student (Student A) has read an article ‘How to survive meeting your partner’s parents for the first time’ (tips: do some homework before you go; be ready to answer questions about yourself; if you are invited for a meal, eat everything and offer to help with the washing-up; be yourself but don’t talk about religion and politics; avoid embarrassing silences – ask what your partner was like as a child). First listen while the student tells you the five tips with details; react and ask a short question now and then. Then you tell the student five tips from your article ‘How to survive a first date (and make a success of it)’, one at a time, with a detail each, using the infinitive with to (e.g. Try to arrive on time. It’s important not to talk about your ex. Decide where to go before the date. Remember to ask questions and listen. Offer to pay half.). At the end, ask which tip from each article is the most important and agree on one. If the student forgets to in an infinitive (e.g. it’s important be…), repeat the phrase correctly in your next reply.
exercises.goal: Tell your partner five tips and choose the most important one.
exercises.opener: Hi! You read about meeting your partner’s parents, right? Tell me the tips.
criteria: tells at least four of the five tips from the article, with a detail each
uses the infinitive with to correctly (try to…, it’s important to…, don’t forget to…)
reacts to the partner’s tips
says which tip is the most important and why

steps.text: Tell the first tips: homework, questions about yourself
steps.example: First, do some homework before you go. Ask your partner where his parents work.

steps.text: Tell the tips about the meal and being yourself
steps.example: If they invite you for a meal, it’s important to eat everything. Try not to talk about politics.

steps.text: Tell the last tip about silences
steps.example: If the conversation is dying, ask what your partner was like as a child.

steps.text: Listen to your partner’s first date tips
Say which tip is the most important
steps.example: I think the most important tip is to be yourself.

reference.title: Weak form of to
reference.text: to is usually unstressed and pronounced /tə/: I want to come. It’s difficult to say. Try not to be late.

reference.title: Linking words with the same consonant sound
reference.text: When a word ends in a consonant sound and the next word begins with the same sound, we often link the words together and only make the consonant sound once. This happens when a word ends in /t/ before to, so, e.g. want to is pronounced /ˈwɒntə/.

tasks.context:
How to survive your first day in a new office
Everybody gets nervous on their first day at any job, but these tips can help you to get it right…
6.30 Wake up early, have breakfast, wash, and get dressed. Wear smart work clothes, but not too smart. Check the weather forecast to make sure your clothes are right, and if you’re driving, check traffic reports to see if there are any problems. TOP TIP: 1 ___
8.50 Plan to arrive at least ten minutes early, but not more than 20 – you don’t want to look too enthusiastic. Say hello to people, smile, and use this time to ask questions. TOP TIP: 2 ___ If you can’t, admit it and say ‘Sorry, I’ve forgotten your name.’
11.00 Offer to make coffee or to bring water for your colleagues. TOP TIP: 3 ___ If it’s very bad, people will always remember it. If it’s very good, they’ll always ask you to make it.
12.00 Don’t be the first person to ask about lunch. Wait to see what everybody else does. TOP TIP: 4 ___
13.00 Be prepared to have problems. Many bosses give new employees some difficult work on their first day to see how they manage. TOP TIP: 5 ___ If you can’t, don’t be afraid to ask for help.
15.00 If you go to a meeting, listen, keep quiet and take notes. TOP TIP: 6 ___ You don’t want to annoy other people on day one.
17.00 Don’t think that staying late will impress your boss. It won’t, at least not on your first day. Go home. TOP TIP: 7 ___ If you made any mistakes, make sure you don’t make them again tomorrow.

exercises.opener: Have you ever had a problem on your first day in a new job, or in a new class or school?
criteria: describes a first day and the problem clearly
uses past tenses correctly
says how they felt and what happened next
asks the partner about his or her first day

steps.text: Say where and when your first day was
steps.example: It was my first day at university, three years ago.

steps.text: Say what the problem was and how you felt
steps.example: I couldn’t find the classroom and I was really nervous.

steps.text: Ask your partner about their first day
steps.example: What about you? Have you ever had a problem like that?

tasks.instruction: Write a How to survive… article. Choose a title, and write at least four tips in a logical order. Start each one with an imperative. Then explain why
tasks.note: SB 5 Writing (в паре в книге → самостоятельно)

exercises.prompt: Write a How to survive… article: How to survive a job interview, a party where you don’t know anyone, or a family holiday. Write at least four tips in a logical order. Start each one with an imperative (Don’t be late. Wear the right clothes…), then explain why.

questions.text: Tip 1: what should you do first? Why?
questions.hint: (Decide… the night before. It’s important to…)

questions.text: Tip 3: what shouldn’t you do? Why?
Tip 4: what should you do at the end?

criteria: a title and at least four tips in a logical order
each tip starts with an imperative (positive or negative)
each tip has a reason
uses the infinitive with to correctly (try to, remember to, it’s important not to)
